neet_che_u20_t05_1.working: Dilute H2SO4 is used because it does not react with KMnO4. HCl is oxidised to Cl2, and HNO3 is itself an oxidising agent.

neet_che_u20_t05_2.working: Equivalents of Fe2+ = 20 × 0.1 × 1 = 2 meq. KMnO4 normality = 0.02 × 5 = 0.1 N, so V = 2/0.1 = 20 mL.

neet_che_u20_t05_3.working: Oxalic acid gives 20 × 0.05 × 2 = 2 meq. Setting 25 × M × 5 = 2 gives M = 0.016 M.

neet_che_u20_t05_4.working: Equivalent weight of KMnO4 in acid = 158/5 = 31.6 (I). n-factor of oxalic acid = 2 (II). n-factor of Fe2+ = 1 (III). n-factor of KMnO4 in acid = 5 (IV).

neet_che_u20_t05_5.working: A is true and B is true. C is false: oxalic acid is warmed, not Mohr's salt, since Fe2+ would be air-oxidised. D is false: KMnO4 is not a primary standard. E is true: Mn2+ autocatalyses the reaction.
